result.keywords: This article describes a field-deployable lighting and imaging method for nocturnal coral reef surveys using low-impact spectral beacons and synchronized camera traps. The approach emphasizes habitat monitoring, species visibility, and thermal neutrality in shallow-water environments. Unlike laboratory tracking, educational software studies, or microfluidic analytics, the work focuses on marine ecology instrumentation and conservation sampling. Measurements are evaluated across multiple reef sites with attention to color fidelity, battery endurance, and disturbance reduction.
result.title: Tidal Lanterns for Coral Reef Night Surveying.
